question: Which renderers support multisample antialiasing (MSAA)?
expected_answer: Only the Forward+ and Mobile renderers; it is not available in the Compatibility renderer.
evidence_quote: This is only available in the Forward+ and Mobile renderers, not the Compatibility renderer.

question: Which project setting do I change to enable MSAA?
expected_answer: Rendering > Anti Aliasing > Quality > MSAA 3D
evidence_quote: MSAA can be enabled in the Project Settings by changing the value of the Rendering > Anti Aliasing > Quality > MSAA 3D setting.

question: What antialiasing option is usually the only viable one when targeting mobile or integrated graphics?
expected_answer: FXAA (2x MSAA may be usable in some circumstances).
evidence_quote: When targeting low-end platforms such as mobile or integrated graphics, FXAA is usually the only viable option.

question: What does calling call_group on the scene tree do?
expected_answer: It calls the given function on every member of the named group.
evidence_quote: The above code calls the function enter_alert_mode on every member of the group guards.

question: If a Global group and a Scene group share the same name, are they separate groups?
expected_answer: No. Groups with the same name are considered one and the same; the distinction is purely organizational.
evidence_quote: The same underlying logic is used for both Global and Scene groups. Groups with the same name are considered one and the same.

question: What is the largest custom mouse cursor image allowed when the game runs in a browser?
expected_answer: 128x128 pixels on the web platform.
evidence_quote: On the web platform, the maximum allowed cursor image size is 128×128.

question: Why is faking a cursor by moving a Sprite2D around worse than the built-in custom cursor?
expected_answer: It adds at least one frame of latency compared to a hardware mouse cursor.
evidence_quote: moving a Sprite2D to the cursor position in a _process() method, but this will add at least one frame of latency compared to a "hardware" mouse cursor.

question: Which languages does Godot officially offer for gameplay programming?
expected_answer: GDScript, C#, and C and C++ via GDExtension.
evidence_quote: Godot offers four gameplay programming languages: GDScript, C#, and, via its GDExtension technology, C and C++.

question: Can a Godot 4 project written in C# be exported to the web?
expected_answer: No, projects written in C# using Godot 4 currently cannot be exported to the web platform.
evidence_quote: Projects written in C# using Godot 4 currently cannot be exported to the web platform.

question: What is the advantage of detaching a scene with remove_child compared with just hiding it?
expected_answer: It is much easier to show/hide: you only call add_child/remove_child instead of tracking several changes.
evidence_quote: Pro: This variation of "hiding" it is much easier to show/hide. Rather than potentially keeping track of multiple changes to the scene, you only need to call the add/remove_child methods.

question: When I switch scenes with the built-in change scene functions, what happens to the old scene?
expected_answer: It is deleted immediately.
evidence_quote: SceneTree.change_scene_to_file() and SceneTree.change_scene_to_packed() will delete the current scene immediately.

question: What kinds of display does Godot support?
expected_answer: Only sRGB and HDR displays.
evidence_quote: However, Godot only supports sRGB and HDR displays.

question: Which collision object leaves all movement and collision response to my own code?
expected_answer: CharacterBody2D (it provides collision detection but no physics).
evidence_quote: A body that provides collision detection, but no physics. All movement and collision response must be implemented in code.

question: Can I count on a physics simulation giving identical results when the same situation is repeated?
expected_answer: No. Godot physics is not deterministic and is not guaranteed to run the same way for seemingly identical situations.
evidence_quote: Physics in Godot, regardless of physics engine, is not deterministic, the nature of physics engine determinism is very complex and has to do with many factors, this means physics is not guaranteed to run the same way for seemingly identical situations.

question: Which input callback is better suited for gameplay input so that the GUI can intercept events first?
expected_answer: Node._unhandled_input()
evidence_quote: For gameplay input, Node._unhandled_input() is generally a better fit, because it allows the GUI to intercept the events.

question: Can a GDScript file inherit from a C# script?
expected_answer: No. A GDScript file may not inherit from a C# script, and a C# script may not inherit from a GDScript file.
evidence_quote: A GDScript file may not inherit from a C# script. Likewise, a C# script may not inherit from a GDScript file.

question: If I call SceneTree.quit directly, can my nodes still finish saving?
expected_answer: No. Quitting that way does not allow custom actions such as saving to complete; send the close-request notification yourself first.
evidence_quote: Quitting by calling SceneTree.quit will not allow custom actions to complete (such as saving, confirming the quit, or debugging), even if you try to delay the line that forces the quit.

question: Which kind of collision shape can only be used inside static bodies?
expected_answer: Concave (trimesh) shapes; they do not work with CharacterBody or RigidBody unless the RigidBody mode is Static.
evidence_quote: You can only use concave shapes within StaticBodies. They will not work with CharacterBodies or RigidBodies unless the RigidBody's mode is Static.

alt_evidence.evidence_quote: You can only use concave shapes within StaticBodies. They will not work with CharacterBodies or RigidBodies unless the RigidBody's mode is Static.

question: Why would an asset referenced with the wrong letter case work on Windows but break on Linux?
expected_answer: Windows and macOS file names are case insensitive, but other platforms such as Linux and Android are case sensitive.
evidence_quote: If a developer working in a case insensitive host file system saves an asset as myfile.PNG, but then references it as myfile.png, it will work fine on their platform, but not on other platforms, such as Linux, Android, etc.

question: How can I reduce textures flickering back and forth in the distance in a 3D scene?
expected_answer: Increase the Camera node's Near property (and decrease Far to the lowest permissible value).
evidence_quote: To make the depth buffer more precise over the rendered area, you should increase the Camera node's Near property.
